question: Should default non-heartbeat runs stop loading HEARTBEAT.md when heartbeat guidance is enabled, or should the current documented normal-run visibility remain the default?
rationale: The source-level optimization gap is clear, but accepting it changes a documented model-facing context contract rather than repairing broken existing behavior.

options.title: Adopt on-demand default
options.body: Make default non-heartbeat runs skip HEARTBEAT.md before load/cache/injection, preserve it for heartbeat runs, update docs, and add focused default/heartbeat regression tests.

options.title: Keep current default
options.body: Leave normal-run HEARTBEAT.md visibility as documented and rely on lightContext or future explicit bootstrap controls for token reduction.

options.title: Fold into broader context policy
options.body: Defer this narrow behavior to the tiered or deterministic bootstrap design so one maintainer decision covers session-type filtering and user controls.

recommendation.title: Adopt on-demand default
recommendation.body: Make default non-heartbeat runs skip HEARTBEAT.md before load/cache/injection, preserve it for heartbeat runs, update docs, and add focused default/heartbeat regression tests.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter has the strongest current history around heartbeat prompt controls and already reviewed this exact default-contract boundary.
